title: Snapshotting node.parentElement inside another feature's teardown window — record a live anchor outside the doomed subtree as restore fallback
trigger: Feature A reparents a shared node and schedules DEFERRED teardown of its wrapper (e.g. exit animation). Feature B mounts inside that window and snapshots `node.parentElement` for later restore — but the snapshot points inside A's wrapper, which A's timer then detaches. B's restore inserts the node into a dead subtree: the node vanishes from the page permanently.
principle: A parentElement snapshot is only valid if the parent outlives the snapshot. When the parent may belong to another feature's pending teardown, record a LIVE anchor outside that subtree at snapshot time (the doomed wrapper's own parent/nextSibling). On restore: use the snapshot if `parent.isConnected`, else fall back to the live anchor. Draining A's pending restore before B mounts is not sufficient — mount ordering puts B's snapshot between A's cleanup-schedule and A's timer fire; the live anchor covers that gap.

cases.context: Player Mode mounts while Split View's 410ms close-restore is still pending. PM snapshots `player.parentElement` = the split-view stageCell (still connected at that instant). The timer then removes the wrapper, detaching stageCell. PM exit-restore calls `originalParent.appendChild(player)` into the detached stageCell → video gone from the page, `findPlayerContainer()` returns null, split view stuck open forever.

applyFor: Any feature that snapshots a DOM position (parentElement/nextSibling) for later restore while other features may reparent or teardown the same subtree
Exit-restore paths of overlays/modes that move a shared node (player, panel) — always guard `parent.isConnected` and keep a live fallback anchor
Entering a mode during another mode's deferred cleanup window
